issues.legal_issue: A joint lessee’s acquisition of only part of the lessor’s interest does not merge or extinguish the lease when the interests in the tenancy and reversion do not fully coincide.
material_facts: The village had originally been granted under one lease, whose interest later devolved among several branches of lessees.
One branch held an eight-anna share of the leasehold and acquired an eight-anna share of the proprietary interest, while other persons continued to hold the remaining interests.
The entire proprietary interest was later sold for unpaid government cess, and the purchasers claimed that the leasehold share had merged into the proprietary interest and passed with it.
The claimants did not allege a fresh contract that extinguished or replaced the existing tenancy.
issues.conclusion: The leasehold interest did not merge into the acquired proprietary share, and the later sale of the proprietary interest did not transfer that leasehold interest to the purchasers.
issues.legal_principle: Merger requires the lessee’s and lessor’s interests to coincide; acquiring only part of the reversion does not extinguish a lease held jointly with others. The Court applied the doctrine of merger and relied on the principle concerning joint tenants’ common obligations discussed in White v. Tyndall (13 App. Cas. 263). No statutory provision was relied on.

rule.if: merger_based_rent_suit_challenge and lease_created_as_single_contract and joint_leasehold_remained_with_others and acquiring_lessee_did_not_own_entire_reversion and no_fresh_contract_severed_interests

predicates.merger_based_rent_suit_challenge: In a dispute over a rent claim, a party challenges the claim on the ground that acquiring a lessor’s interest extinguished the lease.
predicates.lease_created_as_single_contract: The lessor originally granted the property under one lease, and the leasehold later devolved among multiple holders.
predicates.joint_leasehold_remained_with_others: The lessee who acquired a proprietary interest continued to hold the leasehold jointly with other lessees.
predicates.acquiring_lessee_did_not_own_entire_reve: The lessee acquired only part of the lessor’s interest, while other holders retained the rest.
predicates.no_fresh_contract_severed_interests: No fresh agreement between the relevant holders and the lessor replaced or severed the existing tenancy.

issues.definition: When a rent dispute rests on a claimed merger, and a joint lessee acquires only part of the reversion without a fresh agreement severing the tenancy, the lease is not extinguished by that acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: A partition among joint holders of a tenancy, or among holders of the reversion, does not by itself divide the tenancy or end the holders’ common liability for rent to the lessor.
material_facts: The lessees alleged that they had partitioned the leasehold between themselves and occupied separate portions.

They also alleged a partition among holders of the proprietary interest, but did not allege that the tenancy had been severed as against the lessor or that fresh contracts had created separate tenancies.
The lessor’s successors claimed rent from the raiyats under the existing tenancy.
The Court held that even an inter se partition would not alter the tenancy’s integrity or the lessees’ liability to the lessor.
issues.conclusion: The alleged inter se partitions did not create separate tenancies or reduce the joint lessees’ liability to pay the rent as one tenancy.
issues.legal_principle: Several holders of one tenancy constitute one tenant as against the landlord and remain liable for the common rent; an inter se partition for convenience does not alter the tenancy without a severance recognized by the landlord or a fresh contract. The Court relied on White v. Tyndall (13 App. Cas. 263), which explains that co-tenants under a demise owe one rent, not separate rents.

rule.if: landlord_rent_claim_under_joint_tenancy and interest_holders_partitioned_inter_se and no_landlord_recognized_severance and no_fresh_contract_creating_separate_tenancies

predicates.landlord_rent_claim_under_joint_tenancy: A landlord seeks rent from holders of a tenancy that was held jointly.
predicates.interest_holders_partitioned_inter_se: The joint holders divided possession or enjoyment among themselves without involving the landlord in the division.
predicates.no_landlord_recognized_severance: The holders did not establish that the landlord recognized a division of the original tenancy into separate tenancies.
predicates.no_fresh_contract_creating_separate_tena: The landlord and the holders did not make new agreements creating separate tenancies.

issues.definition: When joint holders partition their interests only among themselves and neither the landlord recognizes a severance nor new agreements create separate tenancies, they remain one tenancy with common rent liability.
